Some Notes on the Current Situation (2025)

edges.evidence: Dan Geva and Nuit Geva are a married couple who have collaborated on documentary films since 1994. Both have received NFCT support. A retrospective of their joint work was held at Israeli cinematheques. Nuit Geva's entry in derived_conflicts.json (as 'נוית גבע') is a typo/duplicate of her actual name.

No family connection found. Nadav Lapid's actual brother is Itamar Lapid. The pair (Nadav, Assaf) appears to be a surname-match false positive. Mother was Era Lapid (film editor), father is Chaim Lapid (writer). Assaf Lapid is an unrelated filmmaker.

CONFIRMED BROTHERS. Itamar Lapid is Nadav Lapid's actual brother (confirmed by Ynet obituary of their mother Era Lapid). Itamar co-directed 'איך נתת לזה לקרות' (2021) with Yair Asher. The Israeli Film Fund invested 100,000 NIS in this film (confirmed at filmfund.org.il/Movie?movieId=17). Nadav Lapid served as lector at the Israeli Film Fund in August 2018 — a 3-year gap before Itamar's film was funded. Conflict is PARTIAL: family relationship confirmed, fund support confirmed, but Nadav was not an active lector at the time of Itamar's funding. Check Rabinovich Fund 2021 lectors list for stronger overlap.

Giora Eini (Rabinovich Fund CEO since 1995) and Eti Cohen (head of Film Division, Ministry of Culture 1999-2021) allegedly had a romantic relationship. Cohen allegedly passed insider ministry information to Eini and cancelled Film Council meetings to benefit Rabinovich/Gesher funds. Eini allegedly participated as evaluator in 4 projects against fund rules.

The Adri brothers (Moshe + Leon) received NIS 104,333,500 from Rabinovich + Gesher funds for 85 films (2015-2021), representing 35% of total fund investments. Moshe Adri received 49% of all Rabinovich Fund distributions. They co-own United King production+distribution company and Cinema City. This monopolistic concentration combined with fund relationships is a severe structural conflict.

Yair Raveh (film critic) was allegedly employed as a lector by Giora Eini specifically so he would protect the Rabinovich Fund from negative press coverage. Same allegation applies to Erez Dvorah and Ron Fogel. All three already appear as critics serving multiple fund committees in derived_conflicts.json.

Erez Dvorah (film critic/journalist) was allegedly employed as a lector by Giora Eini for the same reason as Yair Raveh. Dvorah is already in derived_conflicts.json under faculty_committee (gesher) and critic_committee.

Ron Fogel (film critic/journalist) was allegedly employed as a lector by Giora Eini for the same reason as Yair Raveh and Erez Dvorah. Fogel is in derived_conflicts.json (filmfund, makor, rabinovich) as board_member + lector.

Yoav Abramovich served as artistic director for feature films at Rabinovich Fund (2015-2025), then was promoted to CEO (2025). He was allegedly present as evaluator in 26 project applications, violating fund rules. He is also a film producer and screenwriter (Wikipedia), meaning he had financial interests in productions he evaluated.

Amos Kollek (son of Jerusalem Mayor Teddy Kollek) is an active filmmaker (director, screenwriter, actor — films at Cannes 2000, Berlin 2008) AND served as artistic advisor/lector at the Israeli Film Fund (September 2024, Development track). He has historically received fund support. This is a confirmed filmmaker+lector conflict not in derived_conflicts.json.

Udi Yerushalmi was CEO of NFCT 2008-2024, is now listed as a board member (management) of NFCT, AND is a film producer (Beit Tzvi graduate). Triple conflict: former CEO, current board member, filmmaker — all at the same fund. Confirmed by NFCT management page.

Giora Eini (Rabinovich CEO) and Ziv Nave (former Gesher CEO) allegedly met annually at Cannes Film Festival with Eti Cohen (Ministry culture division head) to 'plan Israeli cinema' — coordinating between supposedly independent bodies. This creates a systemic network conflict not visible from individual fund memberships.

Rabinovich Fund CEO Giora Eini allegedly circumvented the lectors evaluation system: when projects involving Moshe Adri were not approved by lectors, Adri was encouraged to appeal, and then Eini personally approved the projects. This mechanism allowed Adri to receive 49% of all Rabinovich Fund distributions (35% of both Rabinovich + Gesher combined). This is a direct CEO-producer preferential funding conflict.

Dorit Enbar (NFCT CEO 2008-2024, now board chair 2025) had her conflict of interest OFFICIALLY RULED by the Knesset Gilaour Committee in 2015 when she was nominated to the Broadcasting Authority council. The committee found she had a conflict because the Broadcasting Authority invests in companies that produce NFCT-supported films. This is the only government-adjudicated conflict of interest in the entire dataset. Source 1 (notification): calcalist.co.il/marketing/articles/0,7340,L-3833615.html. Source 2 (ruling): calcalist.co.il/marketing/articles/0,7340,L-3883770.html

Osnat Bukofzer is employed by the Rabinovich Foundation AND served as Israeli Film Council member for several years. The Film Council oversees and regulates film funds including Rabinovich. She also manages the Israeli Pavilion at Cannes, financed by Rabinovich. As Film Council member, she made decisions directly affecting the amount of money the Rabinovich Fund received — while being employed by that same fund. The filmindustrywatch.org investigation calls this 'a clear case of a conflict of interest.'

Amir Manor served as lector/reader for Israeli Film Fund, Rabinovich Fund, and Gesher Fund (2019-2022). He also received funding for multiple projects including 'הבית ברחוב פין' (Rabinovich grant, 2017). He charges 10,000 NIS for script consulting on projects subsequently submitted to the same funds where he evaluates. Investigation alleges he pre-informed a filmmaker they would 'have to wait for the next round' before submission closed — potential process integrity breach. Triple conflict: lector + recipient + paid consultant to applicants.

Tal Granite and Sharon Maimon are a filmmaking duo who served as lectors for Israeli Film Fund and Rabinovich Fund while also receiving funding for their films. Funded films include 'The Prom' (2018), 'Happy Ending' (2021) - both received fund support while one or both served as evaluators at the same funds. They are also co-directors, making this a joint revolving-door conflict.

Leon Prodovsky served as lector for Israeli Film Fund, Rabinovich, and Gesher funds while also receiving funding. His film 'My Neighbor is Adolf' (2022) received fund support. Appears in the filmindustrywatch.org revolving doors investigation as one of 25 documented cases.

Tawfik Abu Wail served as lector for Israeli Film Fund and Gesher while also receiving funding. His film 'Hassan the Wise' (2019) received fund support. Appears in the filmindustrywatch.org revolving doors investigation.

Kobi Mizrahi served as lector at Gesher, Rabinovich, and Israeli Film Fund while also receiving funding. His film 'Ben Gurion Epilogue' received fund support. Appears in the filmindustrywatch.org revolving doors investigation.

UNVERIFIED. אילנית אדרי serves as Accounting Management (הנהלת חשבונות) at the Israeli Film Fund (confirmed on filmfund.org.il staff page). משה אדרי (producer) received 49% of Rabinovich Fund distributions. Moshe Adri's Wikipedia states he immigrated with 'four siblings' but only names brother Leon. אילנית could be one of those unnamed siblings, but no public source confirms any family connection. The surname אדרי is common among Moroccan Jews. Requires genealogical database access to confirm or deny.

UNVERIFIED. צחי אדרי served as artistic advisor/lector for the Israeli Film Fund in multiple rounds (2019-2023). His profile describes him as a filmmaker/writer working from home while using a wheelchair due to degenerative disease. No public source confirms any family connection to משה אדרי (the producer who received 49% of Rabinovich Fund distributions). If confirmed as a relative, this would be a severe conflict — relative evaluating projects at fund that distributes money to his family's production company.

Shmulik Duvdevani (TAU Steve Tisch School faculty, film critic, lector at NFCT/Rabinovich) reviewed the film 'Nana Dauri' directed by Eti Tsiko (also TAU faculty) giving 4 stars — disclosed relationship only at review's end. He also reviewed 'כביש הסרגל' by Maya Dreifuss (also TAU faculty) with NO disclosure of shared institutional affiliation. Eti Tsiko is also on Jerusalem Film Festival's International Programming Committee. This adds a peer-review-without-disclosure layer to Duvdevani's already-documented conflicts.

Eti Tsiko is both faculty at Tel Aviv University's Steve Tisch School of Film and Television AND serves on the Jerusalem Film Festival's International Programming Committee. As a filmmaker/academic she has institutional interests in which films receive festival placement. Her film 'Nana Dauri' was reviewed (favorably, 4 stars) by her TAU colleague Shmulik Duvdevani without proper disclosure.

Gil Samsonov was appointed chair of the Israeli Film Council (the regulatory body overseeing all film funds) in February 2026 by Culture Minister Miki Zohar. Samsonov's background: (1) Likud party spokesman; (2) Ran on Likud party list for Knesset; (3) Netanyahu campaign advisor in multiple elections; (4) Appointed by Netanyahu government as Broadcasting Authority chair; (5) Partner in advertising firm Glickman Shamir Samsonov (Publicis group); (6) Chair of Advertising Companies Association. He has no professional film background. Appointed by Zohar (Likud coalition) during controversy over film industry awards ceremony. The Film Council oversees how public funds are distributed to film funds — having a political appointee with active commercial/political roles chair this body is a structural conflict.

Avi Nesher (Abi Nesher) is a major Israeli filmmaker who received Rabinovich Foundation production funding. His daughter Tom Nesher received a 1,000,000 NIS grant from the Rabinovich Foundation for her debut feature film 'Sofi Sofi' (later titled 'Karov Elai' / 'Close to Me'). The film was submitted anonymously but critics and the filmindustrywatch.org investigation cite this as a concerning pattern — the daughter of a major fund recipient receiving top-level debut funding. Tom Nesher is confirmed in entity_registry. The film won Best Debut Film at Jerusalem Film Festival and 4 Ophir Awards including Best Film and Best Director 2024.

Dominique Welinski (Dominique Welinski) simultaneously holds two roles: (1) Producer of Yona Rozenkier's films; (2) Curator/consultant for Cannes Film Festival Factory (Directors' Fortnight) and L'Atelier/Residency programs. This gives her direct influence over incorporating Rozenkier's films into Cannes programming while being his producer and financial beneficiary. The Israeli Film Fund granted Rozenkier 2,000,000 NIS (500,000+ EUR) for his next feature — one of only 3 films selected from 100+ applications. The filmindustrywatch.org investigation raises whether Welinski's Cannes connections artificially elevated Rozenkier's perceived international prestige, influencing his fund eligibility. Both persons are in entity_registry.

Ilana Shoshan is simultaneously: (1) Gesher Film Fund board member (since 2018/2020); (2) Co-founder of Signature Productions (international film co-productions, 1992); (3) Film producer ('Joshua Tree' 1992 $10M budget, 'Imaginary Heroes' 2004 starring Sigourney Weaver). As a producer with financial interests in film production, her position on the Gesher Fund board creates a structural exec_filmmaker conflict. She could potentially influence fund decisions in ways that benefit production companies she is affiliated with.

Adar Shafran is head of the Israeli Producers Association (ראש התאחדות המפיקים) — she represents producers' interests in negotiating with film funds. Simultaneously, she received multiple grants from the Rabinovich Foundation as a producer, and from the Israeli Film Fund as a director. This is a triple role conflict: (1) Industry advocate negotiating fund budgets on behalf of producers; (2) Fund recipient as producer; (3) Fund recipient as director. Leading the Producers Association while personally benefiting from fund grants creates a structural conflict between her advocacy role and personal financial interest. Named by filmindustrywatch.org as a documented case of 'control of key people through financial dependence.'

Rami Bezha has been a board member of the Israeli Film Fund since 2016 (9+ years). He is identified as a film/event producer and chair of the 'Independent Forum' (פורום עצמאים) — an industry body. He appeared at the Knesset presenting as 'מפיק' (producer). As a producer serving on the board that funds films, there is a potential exec_filmmaker conflict if he produced films that received Fund investment during his tenure. This requires verification — specific film credits during his board tenure have not been confirmed.

UPDATED (more complete than prior entry): Amir Manor served as lector for: Israeli Film Fund, Gesher Fund, Rabinovich Foundation, and Tel Aviv University — FOUR institutions simultaneously. His funded films: 'Flowers of Marzipan' (2014), 'I Can't Believe I'm a Robot' (2015), 'The House on Finn Street' (2018 Rabinovich grant/2021 release), 'The Swimmer' (2021). This is a QUADRUPLE conflict: (1) lector at 4 institutions; (2) film recipient ×4 projects; (3) paid script consultant (10,000 NIS) to applicants at same funds; (4) allegedly pre-informed an applicant of upcoming submission deadline before it was public. Born December 31, 1979; TAU Film graduate. Wikipedia confirmed.

UPDATED (substantially weakened): אילנית אדרי serves as Accounting Management at the Israeli Film Fund. Moshe Adri has four DAUGHTERS (one named Maia, others unnamed), not sisters, and only ONE named brother (Leon). He immigrated with four siblings total. The name Ilanit does not appear among his daughters in any source. The surname אדרי is common among Moroccan Jews. Probability of family connection very low based on available evidence. Multiple genealogical searches found no connection. Remains technically unverified but assessed as likely coincidental.

Yigal Molad Hayu (Igal Molad Hayu) served as director of the Jerusalem Cinematheque, Israeli Film Archive, AND Jerusalem International Film Festival. He is now chair of the Gesher Film Fund board (since 2025; member since 2020, extended member since 2015). The Cinematheque/JFF and Gesher Fund have a direct cooperative relationship — Gesher supports films screened at JFF and maintains Tel Aviv offices at the Cinematheque. His transition from leading those institutions to chairing the fund that cooperates with them is a classic revolving door. He is not a filmmaker. His conflict is institutional: festival/archive leadership background → fund board chair.

CORRECTED TIMELINE: Assaf Lapid is: (1) FDOC board member for 2024-2026; (2) Director of 'השיבה מהפלנטה האחרת' (2023) which won the FDOC Investigation Prize (פרס התחקיר) at the 2023 ceremony — this was BEFORE his board term, so he was a prize recipient who then joined the board; (3) His film was NOMINATED in the 2024 FDOC Debut Film (סרט ביכורים) competition — this occurred WHILE he was a board member. He was NOT a winner at the 2024 ceremony. The 2024 investigation prize was won by other filmmakers. The conflict structure: (A) former FDOC prize winner who became a board member governing the prize body; (B) sitting board member whose film was in active competition at the organization he governs in the same term. Additionally: serves as Gesher Film Fund lector (2025), creating cross-institutional dual role: FDOC board + Gesher lector. Note: he is NOT the brother of נדב לפיד (prior entries erroneously stated this — this was the false positive finding from Round 1).

Karin Kainer is simultaneously: (1) FDOC board member for 2024-2026; (2) Director of 'טבריה – מתחת לקו האדום' (Tiberias: Below the Red Line, 2023 series) which won the FDOC prize in 2023. The FDOC management page lists her prize win among her board member credentials. She also serves as FDOC's representative to the Israeli Film Academy — a third institutional role. She is a senior lecturer at HIT Holon Institute of Technology, making her an academic, filmmaker, fund prize recipient, and fund board member simultaneously.

UPGRADED FROM PROBABLE TO CONFIRMED: Entity_registry confirms אבי נשר (ID: p_17121a43) has 'lector' role at filmfund, gesher, jerusalem_film_fund, nfct, rabinovich_cinema. תום נשר (ID: p_4b4606de) has sources: edb, rabinovich_cinema — confirming she received Rabinovich Fund support. The filmindustrywatch.org Hebrew investigation (israel-film-industry-alleged-corruption-rabinovich-gesher-funds) explicitly mentions 'the project of Tom Nesher, his father' as an example of alleged preferential Rabinovich Fund support. Tom Nesher received 1,000,000 NIS from Rabinovich for her debut film. She was 'the youngest creator to receive state fund money for a film.' Film 'Close to Me' (previously 'Sofi Sofi') won 4 Ophir Awards 2024 including Best Film and Best Director, and Best Debut at Jerusalem Film Festival. Avi Nesher also assisted her as assistant director on his own film 'Picture of Victory' (2021) — confirmed direct professional collaboration. The specific dates of Avi's lector service vs. Tom's application year require further verification from Rabinovich Fund lector records.

Yoram Levi was an Israeli film/TV producer who founded 'Dana Productions' (דנה הפקות) in 1974, named after his daughter Dana Eden. Dana Eden became one of Israel's leading TV/film producers, producing the series 'Tehran' (טהרן) among others. She passed away in early 2026 during filming of Tehran Season 3 in Greece, aged 52. This is a confirmed father-daughter pair in Israeli film production. However, NO fund conflict was found: no evidence that Yoram Levi served on any film fund committee while Dana Eden's productions received support. The family pair is documented but does not constitute a verified fund conflict of interest.

Katriel Schory founded the Israeli Film Fund and served as CEO for almost 30 years. As one of his last acts as CEO, he approved 1,000,000 NIS in production funding (approved 2018) for the film 'The Last Cinema Show in Bucharest'. The film was directed and produced by Lodi Boken, who owned 51% of the company Balshir International Ltd. Schory's wife, Naomi Schory, owned 49% of the same company. The CEO of the Israeli Film Fund approved a 1M NIS grant for a project directed by his wife's business partner. This is a direct spousal-business-partner conflict of interest. Source article published January 30, 2024 by filmindustrywatch.org.

Efrat Korem served as artistic advisor/lector at the Israeli Film Fund (multiple rounds 2019-2023). Her debut feature film 'Ben Zaken' (בן זקן, 2014) received funding from BOTH the Israeli Film Fund AND the Gesher Film Fund. The film participated in Jerusalem Film Festival 2014, opened the South Film Festival 2014, won the Van Leer Award at the 2013 Jerusalem Pitch event. She is a Sapir College cinema graduate and screenwriter (confirmed at Writers Guild website). The filmindustrywatch.org revolving doors investigation includes her name in the list of 25 documented cases as 'אפרת כורם'. This is a confirmed revolving door: filmmaker funded by Israeli Film Fund + Gesher, then serves as lector at those same funds.

Tzipi Baider simultaneously serves as: (1) FDOC Vice Chair (2024-2026) — governing the Israeli Documentary Forum and its prize process; (2) Gesher Film Fund lector (2025, confirmed on Gesher lectors list). She is also documentary manager at Kastina Communications. The Gesher Film Fund invests in documentary films that are eligible for FDOC prizes. As both FDOC VP and Gesher lector, she makes decisions at both institutions that can affect the same pool of documentary films. Note: Fellow FDOC board member Assaf Lapid is also a confirmed 2025 Gesher Fund lector — meaning TWO FDOC board members serve simultaneously as Gesher evaluators, creating an institutional overlap between the two organizations.

Shmulik Duvdevani is confirmed as: (1) Film critic at Ynet ('מבקר קולנוע של ynet') and 'Muza' (Israel Museum arts journal); (2) Lector at Rabinovich Foundation AND NFCT — explicitly stated in his Wikipedia biography: 'משמש לקטור בקרנות תמיכה לסרטים ישראלים, בהן הקרן החדשה לקולנוע וטלוויזיה וקרן רבינוביץ'; (3) Faculty at TAU Steve Tisch School of Film and Television. He reviewed colleagues' films without proper disclosure: reviewed 'Nana Dauri' by TAU colleague Eti Tsiko with minimal disclosure; reviewed 'כביש הסרגל' by TAU colleague Maya Dreifuss with NO disclosure. Already in derived_conflicts.json as critic_committee for festival_data, filmfund, makor, nfct, rabinovich_cinema.

Yael Shuv is confirmed as: (1) Film critic at Time Out Tel Aviv ('מבקרת הקולנוע שלנו'); (2) Cinema lecturer at Open University; (3) International film festival judge; (4) Gesher Film Fund lector (confirmed in 2018 lectors list at gesherfilmfund.org.il/Page/45/). No evidence found of her as a filmmaker who received fund support. Already in derived_conflicts.json as critic_committee for gesher, makor, nfct, rabinovich_cinema. This entry adds the confirmed Gesher lector source URL.

Neta Shoshani is an FDOC board member for 2024-2026. Her film '1948 – לזכור ולשכוח' (directed by her) was nominated in the 2023 FDOC competition (Feature Documentary category) — this was before her board term. Additionally, she was credited as art designer for a film called 'חידת שושני' which was nominated in the 2024 FDOC Art Design competition — this occurred WHILE she was a board member. The '1948' film previously won the investigative journalism prize at DocAviv 2023. As a board member of FDOC during a competition in which she had professional credits (art design), this creates a conflict between her governance role and her personal professional interest in the competition's outcome.

Assaf Amir (אסף אמיר) has been Chair of the Israeli Film Academy (האקדמיה הישראלית לקולנוע וטלוויזיה) since 2019. Entity_registry (p_378f86c6) lists his roles as: chairperson, creator, lector, producer, screenwriter. As Academy chair he governs the Ophir Awards and Oscar nomination process — while simultaneously being an active film producer and fund lector. His production company Norma Productions received Israeli Film Fund support for 'Givea 24' (2023). His TV series 'Chazarot' (2020) won 8 Academy Awards including Best Series while he chaired the Academy. This is a structural conflict: the head of the body that nominates films for Oscars and gives Ophir Awards is himself an active film producer and fund evaluator.

Esther Vander (אסתר ונדר) is CEO of the Israeli Film Academy (since 2024) AND appears in entity_registry (p_8664d463) with roles: ceo, lector. As Academy CEO she administers the Ophir Awards and Oscar nomination process while simultaneously serving as a fund lector. This creates a conflict: fund evaluator who also runs the awards ceremony that recognizes funded films.

ROUND 6 CONFIRMED SOURCE for existing probable entry. Yair Raveh (יאיר רוה): (1) Film critic/blogger (cinemascope.co.il), (2) former Film Council member, (3) lector at Gesher + NFCT + Rabinovich (confirmed in derived_conflicts.json), (4) his TV series 'קטמנדו' (2012) received Gesher Fund support while he was a Film Council member, (5) explicitly named in filmindustrywatch.org with exact Hebrew quote as one of the journalists Giora Eini employed as lectors to manage press coverage. Source for quid-pro-quo allegation: 'גיורא עיני דאג במשך השנים להעסיק את בכירי העיתונאים לקולנוע בארץ – יאיר רוה, ארז דבורה, רון פוגל, ואחרים, כלקטורים בקרן.' His Wikipedia also confirms: former Film Council member.

ROUND 6 CONFIRMED SOURCE for existing probable entry. Erez Dvorah (ארז דבורה): (1) Film critic at Ynet (since 2007), (2) lector at Rabinovich Foundation — confirmed by his Minshar Arts College CV: 'Rabinovich Foundation, Joshua Rabinovich Foundation for the Arts, 2012, Development and Feature Film tracks', (3) explicitly named in filmindustrywatch.org quid-pro-quo allegation alongside Raveh and Fogel. CV source (Minshar): https://www.minshar.org.il/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/EREZ-DVORAH-CV.pdf. Rabinovich lector start date: 2012.

NEW ANGLE from TheMarker Jan 2, 2026: Moshe Adri served as political operative for Culture Minister Miki Zohar in suppressing filmmaker opposition to Zohar's cinema reform attempts. The article documents that filmmakers who want to 'survive' in the industry must maintain good relations with Adri. This adds a political dimension to the existing monopoly conflict: Adri's power over production/distribution combined with his role as minister's ally creates a dual commercial+political leverage over filmmakers. This is particularly significant because the Zohar reform (abolishing mandatory lectors pool, shifting to commercial metrics) directly benefits large-scale commercial producers like Adri (United King).

ROUND 7 UPGRADE. Assaf Amir is Chair of Israeli Film and Television Academy since 2019 (confirmed: Wikipedia, Haaretz 2025-09-01). He is owner of Norma Productions and active film/TV producer. His production company received Israeli Film Fund support for 'Givea 24' (2023) while he was Academy Chair. His TV series 'Chazarot' (2020, Kan 11) won 8 Israeli Film Academy Awards including Best Series — while Amir CHAIRED the Academy. This is a direct conflict: the Academy Chair's productions compete for and WIN the Ophir and Academy prizes he administers. The entity_registry lector role confirms he also evaluates fund applications. Triple structural conflict: Academy Chair + active producer receiving fund grants + Ophir Award winner during own chairmanship.

ROUND 7 NEW ENTRY. Dorit Enbar served as NFCT CEO for 16 years (2008-2024), then transitioned directly to NFCT Board Chair in 2025. The board oversees management — having the previous 16-year CEO as board chair means the oversight body is chaired by the person whose decisions it should be evaluating. She cultivated all current staff relationships and industry connections as CEO; now she chairs oversight of her successor. Additionally: she had a conflict of interest officially ruled by the Knesset Gilaour Committee in 2015. Source: NFCT management page confirms current board chair role; Globes 2008 confirms CEO appointment.

ROUND 7 CONFIRMED. Ziv Naveh served as CEO and Artistic Director of Gesher Multicultural Film Fund 2005-2025. Prior to this role, she established and ran Ziv Naveh Productions, directing and producing documentary films including: 'Between Two Worlds,' 'Welcome to Hell,' 'Menuhah''s Film,' 'Code of Silence.' She founded the Drama Department at the Israeli Public Broadcasting Corporation (2017). This is a 20-year exec_filmmaker conflict: a documentary filmmaker who ran the fund financing documentary films. Additional allegation: her appointment was connected to political relationship with Hilel Tropper (Culture Minister) whose relative Daniel Tropper co-founded Gesher Fund. Source: bliss-media.co.il bio + filmindustrywatch.org.

ROUND 7 CONFIRMED with complete fund list and dates. Ron Fogel served as lector at: (1) Israeli Film Fund (2014); (2) Ministry of Culture film department (2017); (3) Rabinovich Foundation (2018); (4) Makor Film Fund (2019); (5) Galil Film Fund (2021). He is a film critic at KAN (public TV/radio, since 2007), Seret website, Cinemateque magazine, and Liberal magazine. He is a FIPRESCI member and served as President of FIPRESCI Jury at Cannes 2021 — first Israeli in this role. His film criticism directly affects public perception of the funds and films he evaluates as a lector.
